Marissa, thanks for the materials. Quick clarifications from our side:

1) Liability cap — Acme generally requires a cap equal to the fees paid in the prior 12 months. We understand carve-outs for confidentiality and intentional wrongdoing, but we need consequential damages to be recoverable in cases where Redwood’s outage triggers downstream customer SLAs (we can show examples).

2) Termination and refunds — for the prepaid annual license (we bill annually), we need a pro rata refund if Redwood terminates without cause, and at minimum wind-down assistance (30 days) to migrate traffic out.

We don’t expect Redwood to accept unlimited liability, but the 12‑month fee cap + carve-outs for certain types of damages is our starting point. Can your legal team propose language that preserves our ability to recover consequential losses tied directly to service outages and clarifies what wind-down assistance includes (data handover, export, short-term support)?

Happy to hop on a 20‑minute call if that’s faster.

—Jordan
Chief Legal Officer | Acme Corporation

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA redlines — liability cap and termination items

Marissa / Jordan / Laura — thanks for the recap, Jordan. I reviewed the redlines and here are my recommendations (high level, followed by proposed language).

High-level tradeoffs:
- Cap amount: moving from a 6‑month to a 12‑month fee cap materially increases Redwood’s exposure. We can accept 12 months only if we limit the categories that bypass the cap (e.g., confidentiality breach, willful misconduct, and gross negligence).
- Consequential damages: Acme’s ask to recover consequential damages for "SLA-triggered downstream customer penalties" is broad. We can consider a narrow carve-out that allows consequential damages only where (i) the damages are directly caused by Redwood’s gross negligence or willful misconduct, and (ii) are reasonably foreseeable and documented (e.g., pre-notified penalties tied to specified SLAs).
- Termination / refunds: For prepayments, industry practice is pro rata refunds where the vendor terminates for convenience, less any non‑refundable setup fees and unused credits. We should limit refunds to amounts already paid for unused service period and exclude estimated future benefits.
- Wind-down assistance: define as time-bound (e.g., up to 30 days) and scoped to technical handover tasks (data export in standard formats; access tokens revocation; up to X engineer-hours at standard hourly rate for migration assistance). Unlimited or open‑ended obligations are a non‑starter.

Proposed language (suggested draft you can paste into the MSA):

"Limitation of Liability. Except for liability arising from (a) a party’s breach of its obligations under Section [Confidentiality], (b) willful misconduct, or (c) fraud, each party’s aggregate liability to the other for any and all claims arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the total fees paid or payable by Customer to Provider under the Order Form in the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither party shall be liable to the other for lost profits or indirect, incidental, or punitive damages, except that Customer may recover consequential damages directly caused by Provider’s gross negligence or willful misconduct where such damages were reasonably foreseeable and documented in advance."

"Termination; Refunds and Wind‑Down Assistance. If Provider terminates the Agreement for convenience, Provider shall refund Customer on a pro rata basis for prepaid fees covering the unused portion of the applicable billing period, less any non‑refundable implementation fees and unused credits. Provider shall provide up to thirty (30) days of wind‑down assistance, which shall include reasonable efforts to (i) export Customer data in standard formats, (ii) deliver configuration and integration artifacts, and (iii) provide up to 40 engineer-hours of migration support at Provider’s standard hourly rate. Such assistance shall not include custom development work beyond migration support and shall be subject to Customer’s compliance with Provider’s data export process."

Notes for negotiation:
- We should get Acme to accept the 12‑month cap with those limited carve-outs rather than an open consequential-damages carve-in.
- For the wind-down assistance, the hourly cap and exclusion of custom dev work are important. Consider offering the first 8 hours free as a commercial concession.

Laura — if you want, I can soften the tone around refunds (e.g., offer refund net of a migration fee) before we share.

-Rishi
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Draft MSA redlines — liability cap and termination items

Jordan / Sofia — thanks for the patience. Rishi reviewed and we’ve proposed language that (a) accepts a 12‑month fee cap, (b) limits carve-outs to confidentiality, willful misconduct, and gross negligence, and (c) permits a narrow consequential damages recovery only where gross negligence or willful misconduct caused documented SLA penalties.

On termination: we will provide pro rata refunds for prepaid unused periods if Redwood terminates for convenience, less non‑refundable implementation fees. We’re also offering 30 days of wind‑down assistance (data export + delivery of integration artifacts + up to 40 engineer-hours at standard rate). As a commercial gesture, Redwood will cover the first 8 hours of migration assistance at no charge.

Next steps: if this approach is acceptable, can you confirm by EOD Thurs 3/12 and we’ll prepare a clean MSA for countersign and then DocuSign the Order Form? Happy to take a quick call to walk through the proposed clauses.

Attachments: ACME_MSA_Redlines_v3.pdf (with Rishi’s suggested text inserted).

Best —
Marissa

Marissa / Rishi — thanks, that’s helpful and closer to what we can accept. A few quick asks before we finalize:

- Please add explicit examples in an SOW/Annex that illustrate when consequential damages could be recoverable (e.g., documented SLA penalty assessed by Acme’s downstream customer tied to Provider outage).
- In the wind-down paragraph, please clarify whether "migration support at Provider’s standard hourly rate" is billable to Acme or whether those hours beyond the 8‑hour concession will be discounted.

If you can add those clarifications in the clean MSA, we can circulate internally and plan to countersign next week. I’ll also put the Order Form and DocuSign on our procurement queue.

Jordan
